chunks: From him, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn, from Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl, from Ṣāliḥ ibn ʿUqbah, from Abī Maryam al-Anṣārī, who said:

Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام led us in salat (prayer) wearing a qamīṣ, without an izār, without a ridāʾ, and without adhān or iqāmah. When he finished, I said to him: May Allah grant you well-being, you led us in salat (prayer) wearing a qamīṣ without an izār, without a ridāʾ, and without adhān or iqāmah.

He said: “Indeed, my qamīṣ is thick, so it suffices such that I do not need to have an izār or a ridāʾ upon me. And I passed by Jaʿfar while he was giving the adhān and iqāmah, and I did not speak, so that sufficed for me.”

key_terms.إِزَارٍ: A lower wrap garment mentioned here as not being additionally required.
key_terms.إِقَامَةٍ: The second call signaling the immediate commencement of salat (prayer).
key_terms.رِدَاءٍ: An upper wrap or cloak mentioned here as not being additionally required.
key_terms.قَمِيصٍ: A shirt or tunic worn in prayer.
key_terms.كَثِيفٌ: Thick; indicating a garment dense enough to provide sufficient covering.

ai.seo_question: Is it sufficient to pray in a thick qamīṣ without an izār and ridāʾ, and can another person's adhān and iqāmah suffice?
ai.summary: This hadith reports that Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام led salat (prayer) wearing only a thick qamīṣ and without independently giving adhān or iqāmah. He explained that the thickness of the garment was sufficient coverage, and that hearing Jaʿfar already giving the adhān and iqāmah sufficed for him.
